Subject: SBJ Facilities: ANC-LG tie-up shows an industry’s direction Also: More from the Commanders’ VanHorn  March 23, 2026READ IN BROWSER   I’ll be at SBJ and Leaders in Sports’ Business of Soccer event this week in Atlanta. Please say hello if you’re at the event. If you do, please do not ask about the final 12 minutes of UNC’s opening-round NCAA Men’s Basketball Tournament loss.    (l-to-r) LG VP/Corporate Marketing Chulho Huh; Don Kwack, president and CEO of LG Electronics North America; ANC’s Jerry Cifarelli Jr.; and LG’s John Won, president of media entertainment solutions. ANC-LG relationship ‘fits where the industry is going’ When I joined a call with Jerry Cifarelli and Chulho Huh, they were discussing workout routines. These two get along, which is part of the strength of the relationship between their two companies, LG, the South Korea-based makers of well-known home appliances, and ANC.

In the past, ANC might have been described simply as an LED display provider, Daktronics’ main competitor in the North American pro sports market. They’re a bit more than that, and they are leaning into the differences under Cifarelli, who in 2023 bought the company his father, Jerry Sr., founded in 1997.

ANC is built on three units: tech integration (installing LED displays); ongoing tech service related to those installations; and a media and sponsorship sales business connected to the LED displays. Unlike Dak, ANC doesn’t do any manufacturing and has an asset-light business, and it leans into sponsorship more heavily than its South Dakota-based competitor.

The partnership with LG, which has generated eight to nine figures of business already, according to Cifarelli (an SBJ Forty Under 40 honoree in 2025), is the best vehicle for explaining how those three verticals fit together under one ANC umbrella. 

Originally founded in 1958 under a different name, LG has existed under the “Life’s Good” brand (LG) since the mid-1990s, but it hadn’t seriously waded into the North American sports industry until a 2023 meeting with Cifarelli and ANC in Barcelona.

A deal framework emerged from that meeting in which ANC would be LG’s nonexclusive conduit for LED display sales to North American sports teams and venues, as well as serving as LG’s agency of record in doing sponsorship and marketing deals with the same teams and venues buying the boards.

LG has the No. 1 market share in washing machines and refrigerators, but “we are placing a strategic focus on expanding our B2B business,” Huh said, “and we see ANC as an imperative partner for achieving our vision.”

The LG-ANC deals began with the Red Sox and Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment, and now include the Ravens, Commanders, and Monumental Sports & Entertainment. Acquiring the right to communicate to those teams’ fans was nearly as powerful for LG as their video boards being used in highly public stadiums, like Fenway Park.

The connections that LG is making in the sports industry via ANC is, additionally, helping it make inroads with sales of dishwashers and laundry appliances to those same sports organizations, though that’s not the focus of their deal.

“We’re very proud of this marriage because for us it fits ANC’s business and it fits LG’s business, and it fits where the industry is going,” said Cifarelli.     The Commanders’ planned D.C. stadium will have a promenade that has the look and feel of the nearby the National Mall in D.C.  Commanders, Andy VanHorn building a real-estate network in the NFL I only had a page for my magazine profile of Commanders Head of Real Estate Andy VanHorn, so there were plenty of interesting leftovers that didn’t make it into print. 

Where’s the project right now? 

The Commanders’ D.C. stadium is moving through the design process, with the concept design finished and now roughly halfway through schematic drawings. That work will wrap up in April, with design documents following in late summer or early fall. VanHorn expects the team to break ground in March 2027.

Mixed-use master planning, a process run by the District of Columbia, kicks off next month to determine how the large areas around the stadium will look. Perkins Eastman is the surrounding development’s master planner development architect. 

Hiring specialists

Commanders President Mark Clouse built factories all over the world during nearly 30 years in the food industry, the final six spent as Campbell’s CEO. That construction résumé included one of the world’s largest bakeries, “but it ain’t a stadium,” he noted. Clouse and others I spoke to imagine VanHorn’s role proliferating throughout pro sports.

“The teams that are successful are the ones that are going to recognize that just because you are an expert in sports doesn’t mean you’re an expert in real estate,” Clouse said. “If you’re going to spend over several billion dollars, it’s worth it to invest in some talent. This was an easy one for me.” 

A powerful network 

An unofficial group of executives working on NFL stadium projects has convened in recent months, including VanHorn, Clouse and the Commanders. Every league meeting, they end up in a room together, asking, “OK, what have you learned?” said Clouse.

“It is a really powerful network.” 

How to structure the project team has been a constant source of discussion. The Commanders have roughly a hundred people working on their stadium project, led by the 40 to 50 from the lead architecture firm, HKS. CAA Icon and Brailsford and Dunlavey provide roughly another dozen project support people, while the Commanders, including VanHorn, have a seven-person internal team. 

“We’re developing a good playbook for what it looks like. It’s going to become an ever-growing part of sports. I think you’ll likely see this in most teams. Even if they’re not building a stadium, even if it’s not in place today, it’s what most are aspiring to,” Clouse said, referring to the broader real estate portfolios that many NFL teams are assembling. 

The exposure of a role with the Commanders 

VanHorn was integral to Arlington, Va., attracting Amazon’s HQ2, but that project was really for the people inside the building, he said. The Commanders’ stadium is for the fans and the community. Millions of people pay attention to it. Every rendering release generates huge debate. 

“And they’re going to take a picture of this one. No one goes and takes a picture of Amazon,” said VanHorn. “The exposure here is significantly higher.” 

Clouse was involved with press and investors while at Campbell’s, but not with the general public. I asked him how he and VanHorn had adapted to being in the spotlight.

“The short answer is we are not anxious to be in the spotlight,” Clouse said, smiling. He noted that, as we spoke, VanHorn was at a gathering discussing the stadium project. “If these are things that we think are going to help us in attracting the right partners, creating the right awareness around the project, then we’re going to do it. 

“People were really passionate about soup, but it doesn’t compare to how they feel about their football team. And the stadium in particular is such a source of joy, excitement, and to a certain degree of return to something that so many fans had been waiting for. What a gift to be able to work on something that makes people feel that way,” said Clouse.  Andy VanHorn’s real estate experience and expertise were needed by the Commanders, who are juggling roughly $10 billion-worth of real estate.     Daps has pivoted to narrowing its business model on in-venue experiences. Daps’ focus narrows to in-person experiences SBJ has written about Daps several times over the last few years, and I checked in with them again after the company (formerly known as Daps Bounty) shed another layer (and word in its name) to reveal a narrower focus.

Daps — as in the handshake you do with your nephew when you’re trying to project “cool” — had created a platform where fans could suggest something they wanted from a favorite athlete, offer how much they would pay for that thing or experience, and wait to see the player’s response. 

Unfortunately for me, I found out about Daps too late to make my offer: paying one of LaMelo Ball’s speeding tickets if he would play Magic: The Gathering with me. (jk)

Instead, the offers that Daps continually received steered the company in a specific direction: in-person experiences before or after live sporting events, what co-founder Jake Klores described as “‘holy s***’ moments with the people they admire.”

The narrowed focus also likely speaks to athletes’ lack of desire to, for example, eat dinner with a fan they’ve never met. Limiting interactions to the sports venues where athletes already do their jobs probably increases the likelihood of athletes accepting “bounties.”

The company has also moved away from simply providing bidders with a collectible devoid of an interaction. The experiences — the moment with the athlete, no matter how fleeting — are the collectibles. 

“As digital entertainment becomes more and more abundant, real world, physical experiences are only going to become more sought after,” Klores said.

To be clear: If a bidder’s request for a game-worn jersey from a player is approved, it’s on the bidder to get into the game with their own ticket; Daps is just facilitating the exchange. 

Daps has had conversations with teams and leagues, but it mainly arranges these experiences at events by going through the player or their representation. The new iteration of Daps, mostly focused on the NBA, WNBA, college basketball and even high school basketball, emerged from private beta roughly a month ago. Daps plans to get into more sports down the line.

“Right now, we’re heads-down focused on as narrow a value prop as we can add,” said Klores.     Would you eat this? The Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo takes over NRG Park for the next month. Aramark Sports + Entertainment is offering this souvenir frozen margarita ($17.95) and a loaded BBQ tots cowboy hat ($18.99). Giddyup!      Big idea Sticking with the Texas theme, take whatever metaphorical business lessons away from this Smithsonian Magazine story about guard dogs on Central Texas ranches that you need to, but I enjoyed this story for several reasons: I love dogs, written descriptions of the American West, and that these guardian dogs’ work happened out of sight and almost never involved direct conflict with the coyotes.      Facilities speed reads

Description:
To: alexg@anc.com; matthew.hobbs@anc.com
CC: steve@crescendolimited.com
BCC: 
Attachment: --none--

Subject: KSP Pricing Feedback
Body:
Hi Alex, Matt,
Thank you for all of your time today! I'm going to send the discussed documents shortly, but I wanted to send the pricing feedback under a separate email since it's lengthy. Feel free to let me know if you have any questions or want to discuss. If there's anything you think we should double-check with Daktronics to ensure a fair comparison, I'm happy to do that too. 
Second email coming soon!Alycia
HOLLYWOOD PARK- Level 8 Pylons: Display costs are significantly different (i.e., millions).- Concessions: Display costs are higher. Of the top 10 most expensive signs for each bidder under this section, seven screens are among both bids top 10. Overall, ANC's screens are consistently higher anywhere from 30%-50%. While no single screen is significantly higher than the others, $30K-$50K per screen across fifty screens adds up.- YTT: ANC's display costs are 40–50% higher for the Stage screen, but your AA Plaza #1 is significantly lower. Interestingly, though, each bidder's combined cost for the two screens is approximately the same. So, we may need to investigate these two screens further. Outside of those two, your House L, House R, Level 2 and Level 4 are approx. 50% higher. 
BALL ARENAThis is where I know it's not apples-to-apples because we're not comparing the same pixel pitches for all screens (hence the recent request). See the pixel pitch comparison below - ANC's is on the left. - Voms: 3.9 vs 5.9- Club lines: 10 vs 10- Chip: 10 vs. 5.9- Fascia 10 vs. 10- Voms 1-4: 10 vs. 5.9- Player Tunnels: 10 vs. 5.9- Your installation cost for Player Tunnels is significantly higher. The subframes, drawings, CMS onboarding & equipment disposal line items are all slightly higher, but the real difference is Electrical & Data Wiring. If I'm not mistaken you had some challenges getting a timely quote from a local electrician? So that may be the issue here.- For the Ball Arena Center Hung 2.0, what assumptions were used for the cost projection? Since this is a hypothetical design at this point I want to ensure we are clear on the assumptions used to reach that number.  E.g., square feet, number of faces, etc. 
DSGP- South Scoreboard: Installation costs. Same as the Player Tunnels comment above (Electrical & Data Wiring).- West Fascia: Display and installation costs are higher. For installation, the most significant differences involve electrical components, subframes, and display costs.  
-- 
Alycia Tanzini
E: alycia@crescendolimited.com

Subject: Re: ANC audio issues at Rutgers Softball
Body:
Jake, 

We have been working to resolve the issues here at both softball and baseball. We believe there are no longer any issues with Dante itself, however, we are seeing a recurrent issue of the hybrid player muting. When we login remotely the hybrid player mutes. If this player is muted the audio will not play. By chance do you know if anyone from Rutgers is logging in remotely. If so, this would cause audio to mute. A way to prevent this would be to login to the backup hybrid player and connect to the primary from there.

To check for this issue when coming into the laptop, the person would need to VNC into the hybrid player from the laptop and check if sound is muted in the volume mixer. If muted, they would just need to unmute, and this will resolve the issue with sound. I am available to walk those individuals through this check.

Thanks  

Miguel Sangester
Regional Manager

Body:
Hi all, 
Please see minutes and next steps below: 
OBM x Sunset Cinema – Curtain Structural ReviewMeeting Minutes
Date: March 20, 2026

1. DesignDWS presented three curtain design options:Two previously developed schemesA third option (referred to as the “Louvre version”) introduced in response to design feedbackAll three options were reviewed during the meeting.Initial feedback:The Louvre version addresses the desire for increased dynamism at the bottom edgeHowever, there is concern that the header condition may not align with the owner’s original design intentNext design coordination:Further feedback on all 3 models will be gathered during the Monday design call with an eye towards narrowing options. DWS to upload all three models to Dropbox in advance of that meeting for team review2. Engineering ApproachHoward (Seattle Structural) proposed a key shift in approach:Decouple the curtain system from the base structureAllow DWS to design and fabricate the curtain as a self-contained systemSeattle Structural would then:Develop the attachment strategy back to the primary structureBenefits of this approach:Enables DWS to work more independently and efficientlyAllows for larger prefabricated sectionsSupports a more streamlined “plug-and-play” / lift-and-bolt installation strategySimplifies coordination between systems by reducing interdependenciesAdditional notes:The leading edge condition remains tight, but this approach allows DWS to take ownership of resolving that interface to some degree.DWS aligned that this is a strong and viable direction forwardDWS/Seattle Structural discussed capacity and loads 
3. Next StepsDWS (Weekend Work Leading into Monday Call)Surface Models for Design ReviewDevelop and upload surface-only models for all three design optionsPurpose: enable focused review of form, flow, and visual intent independent of structureStructural Connection DevelopmentDevelop structural connections, aligned with the decoupled system approach

D            Aura Infield Ribbon during both inning breaks and game play. During game play, it will be displayed in the 486x90 section. Due to MLB rules,

F             Main Video Board during game play only. Due to MLB rules, this creative
MUST be as still. The creative will play in the 2944x294 section.
J              Truly Terrace (Left) during both inning breaks and game play. During game play, it will be displayed in the 350x90 section. Due to MLB rules,
 this creative MUST be as still. During inning breaks, your content will play in the 1520x90 section. This creative can be either an animation or still.
 
Please see attached for the content creation pages.

Friday, March 13th.

Thank you and I look forward to working with you this season!

Can you do the math and tell me what the linear feet are for 5700 pixels?  I know sponsorship will need to know that.

The remaining pixels of that outside section (3900) will be scores.
The middle section on the other side of BoA (15220 pixels) will be a combination of scores and line score.

Animations for headshots, etc, will run the full 9600 pixels at the ends and 15220 pixels for the middle.

We will call the Reserve spaces the following:
Reserve Left / Right (90x9600 each)
Reserve Rotational Left / Right (90x5700 each)
Reserve Outside Scores Left / Right (90x3900)
Reserve Permanent Ad Left/Right (90x1310)
Reserve Middle (90x15220)
This middle section will also be scores (3900 pixels on each side) but then will have a line score, mound visits and challenges remaining.
We will create 3 windows.  2 that are 3900 pixels for the scores so it matches the other window on the outside of BofA and then a middle section that is 7420 pixels that will have the line score.
They will be called:
Reserve Inside Scores Left / Right (90x3900)
Reserve Middle Line score (90x7420)

I know that’s a lot but it makes the most sense to me breaking it up in this manner so we can script it accordingly.

Let me know your thoughts.

Reserve:
We are getting closer for the Reserve level boards.
You gave us all the dimensions for the BofA windows and 3 other windows, but we will be creating a Reserve Rotational space at the ends of the boards, closest to the foul pole.
I know that the space from the end to the BofA sign is 9600 pixels.
The Ad space (Rotational) will be the last 90x5700 pixels on both sides.
Can you do the math and tell me what the linear feet are for 5700 pixels?  I know sponsorship will need to know that.
 
The remaining pixels of that outside section (3900) will be scores. 

The middle section on the other side of BoA (15220 pixels) will be a combination of scores and line score. 

 
Animations for headshots, etc, will run the full 9600 pixels at the ends and 15220 pixels for the middle.
 
We will call the Reserve spaces the following:
Reserve Left / Right (90x9600 each)
Reserve Rotational Left / Right (90x5700 each)
Reserve Outside Scores Left / Right (90x3900)
Reserve Permanent Ad Left/Right (90x1310)
Reserve Middle (90x15220)
This middle section will also be scores (3900 pixels on each side) but then will have a line score, mound visits and challenges remaining.
We will create 3 windows.  2 that are 3900 pixels for the scores so it matches the other window on the outside of BofA and then a middle section that is 7420 pixels that will have
 the line score.
They will be called:
Reserve Inside Scores Left / Right (90x3900)
Reserve Middle Line score (90x7420)
 
I know that’s a lot but it makes the most sense to me breaking it up in this manner so we can script it accordingly.
 
Let me know your thoughts.
 
Thanks,
Tom

Rob and Matt, Thanks for participating in the call with the Zenith engineering team at LG this week. Wanted to follow up and circle back on a couple of open items and engage your thoughts as it relates to what is needed specifically to support the proposed Ventura OS from LG. For background purposes, much effort has been asserted behind the scenes in advance of the call.  The conversation to pursue this with LG grew out of an initial casual conversation with Jehan on price targets and aspirations.  Subsequent to this, we have had several meetings within LG US ID as well as LG HQ in Seoul which led to a recent follow up meeting with Jehan and the head of the US ID unit. As evidenced, the concept of moving away from LG’s WebOS is not embraced by all of LG and for the benefit of Trade Desk and its Ventura OS aspirations this is a unique and isolated opportunity for BILT specifically not a wholesale corporate initiative as LG’s strategy and aspirations within the CTV channel as well as the advancement of the LG WebOS solution is paramount to their long-term strategy. Also for your benefit, the purpose of the call this week was to explore if the 2.0 version of what LG is in the process of executing on behalf of one their major global partners could be expanded and leveraged together.  Based upon the initial feedback, this does not appear to be plausible but welcome your point-of-view and feedback. If so and in the effort to maintain forward momentum, if you can provide your specific technical specifications to support Ventura OS and a road map, we can then work to tackle the needs outside of the LG engineering team unless required to fulfill the BILT objectives. On the business end (again casual) Jehan and I discussed a solution to a revenue share model between BILT and LG in return for the accommodation of an LG significantly discounted price on the units.  I’m sure you can appreciate, this is largely based upon the significant commitment by BILT to deploy across their unique customer base, work to monetize and leverage their customer base inside and outside of the home working with their partners, ambitious strategic growth objectives, etc. as well as align across LG’s other products and solutions with BILT and its partners. Another item that would be helpful is clarification or insights on how the Ventura approach could impact or impair LG’s relationship with Google as the Ventura OS appears to utilize Android foundations and the implications of this could both be a potential conflict with Google’s ecosystem strategy as well as LG’s relationship with Google. Here to help in any way as we are fully committed to the LG/ BILT partnership as this is just one of several initiatives. Alex    Alex GomezSVP, RelationshipsM: (917) 547-9499alexg@anc.com

Subject: Email: Control room for discussion
Description:
To: matthew.hobbs@anc.com; alexg@anc.com
CC: nigel.roberts@lge.com
BCC: 
Attachment: --none--

Subject: Control room for discussion
Body:
 Hi Matt, Following on from earlier conversation please see some thoughts on the Control room equipment for discussion that may or not be used and integrated with your operating equipment I know that there is somewhat a blank slate for this project, and the focus is on what's going to give the biggest impact in terms of the fan / customer experience, whilst also being flexible to cater for different configurations and levels of technical control.  We had previously  discussed a central operation/control room with the ability to:  Take in 15+ live video inputs at any one time Be flexible in routing of the video signals Be able to support the latest standards - so ideally a 4K60p capable system Offer recording capabilities, be it a program output or ISO recordingsOffer the live streaming Offer live replay Be able to run a mixed production, with the ability of overlaying the likes of customers/VIP logos on screen etcBe able to feed in the likes of a presentation feed for the VIP / event areas Be able to run a production for the VIP / Event areas Have traditional professional control over the system, yet also have a more accessible means to control for non technical staff Be able to control the system elsewhere on the premises  Key brands we discussed on that I have looked at. Blackmagic DesignBlackmagic could be a good fit for this type of project, as they offer a comprehensive ecosystem that can cover the likes of: video routing, standards conversion, IP distribution, production switchers, control surfaces, live replay, recording, streaming, and storage. It's a modular approach to a production system, which makes for easier scaling should the system need to grow in future - you can upgrade the individual elements.  IP routing: Blackmagic 2110 IP Converter 8x12G SFPBlackmagic Design 2110 IP Converter 8x12G SFP - HoldanGiven the amount of sources we want  to route from around the stadium to the operator room, it would make sense to try and utilise fibre for the transmission, Blackmagic have a range of 2110 converters with fibre capability, whether it be stand alone at camera locations to convert from SDI to 2110 and fibre, or rack mount systems that would sit in the control room such as the one above that can convert up to 8 streams simultaneously - you'd likely need a few of these units to be able to decode back to SDI in the operator room to feed into the Videohub below.  Video routing: Blackmagic Videohub 80x80 12GBlackmagic Design Videohub 80x80 12G - HoldanThis is a 80 input 80 output video router supporting up to 4K60p on every input and output. There is a frame sync on every input, and it can handle a mixture of resolutions and frame rates simultaneously. It can also be remotely controlled over the network, so users can recall preset configurations with ease.  Video Switching: Blackmagic ATEM 4M/E Constellation 4K Blackmagic Design ATEM 4 M/E Constellation 4K - HoldanThis is a full production switcher system, that can handle 40 x 4K60p inputs , all with frame sync and scaling on the inputs should a resolution be fed into it below the master system res and frame rate. It also has 24 independent outputs, so is also flexible in routing. You'll be able to run a fully switched production from this unit, along with split screens, PiPs, along with graphics and logo overlays etc.  Video Switching Control: ATEM 1M/E Advanced Panel 30 Blackmagic Design ATEM 1 M/E Advanced Panel 30 - HoldanControl interface for the ATEM unit, this is a 1M/E panel for up to 30 live inputs - but you can toggle between other M/Es should you need quick access to them - These act as a separate independent bus.  Recording Decks: Hyperdeck Studio 4K Pro Blackmagic Design Hyperdeck Studio 4K Pro - HoldanThese can take in up to 4K60p over SDI, and record to onboard SSDs, however given the number of streams you may want to record simultaneously, it would be a cleaner solution to have these encode and record directly to the Blackmagic Cloud Store NAS listed below:   NAS Storage: Cloud Store Max 48TBBlackmagic Design Cloud Store Max 48TB - HoldanThis needs 10G network infrastructure to be able to handle multiple 4K60p streams for recording, however it does mean that all recordings would be centrally stored on the one NAS RAID.  Live Replay: Multiple Blackmagic products to do this: Host computer running Davinci Resolve which has a live replay function built into it. This host machine can see the video files as they are being written to the NAS storage. Blackmagic Design UltraStudio 4K Mini - Holdan - This allows the host computer to output the video replay over SDI, or even graphics with transparency back into the production system to be taken live. Blackmagic Design DaVinci Resolve Replay Editor - Holdan - This is what the operator uses to control Resolve running on the host PC quickly and with ease. This computer would need at minimum a 10G connection to the network infrastructure, we have a range of 10G NICs either PCIe based or desktop based that can offer this connectivity such as this: Sonnet Twin 10G - Thunderbolt 3 Edition - Holdan Live Streaming Encoder: Streaming Encoder 4K Blackmagic Design Streaming Encoder 4K - HoldanSimple and cost effective live streaming encoder. You could route any source, or any output from the likes of the videohub or ATEM to this unit to go live directly to a content platform, or simply output via UVC to go into the likes of VC platforms like teams etc.  DensitronAll the above can be controlled through Blackmagic software or hardware devices, done so in a way that is akin to traditional production. For condensed and simplified controlled, or should a certain level of automation be needed we could use Densitron. Their pedigree is creating control systems for broadcast environments, which can be as simple as a single push button device, or a range of touchscreen interfaces distributed around the premises. IDS Software | Device Management Broadcast Control System - Densitron Once we know the full requirements of what they want to be able to achieve to be able to start formalising an end-to-end system, which could be from the above list or similar based on what's needed. However I hope the above gives you a good idea as to what could be possible with a BMD system, and the flexibility it can present.  Look forward to chatting through. Best Regards Scott     Scott Maitland  07974224761Account Directorscott @ssuk.co.ukSSUK45 Queen Elizabeth AvenueGlasgow, G52 4NQ0141 810 4111www.ssuk.co.ukThis message and any attachments are intended for the individual to whom they are specifically addressed to above.  the line score.

Reserve Inside Scores Left / Right (90x3900)

MUST be as still. The creative will play in the 2944x294 section.
J              Truly Terrace (Left) during both inning breaks and game play. During game play, it will be displayed in the 350x90 section. Due to MLB rules, this
 creative MUST be as still. During inning breaks, your content will play in the 1520x90 section. This creative can be either an animation or still.

Friday, March 6th. If you have any questions at all, please reply all.

Hi Jim,
I got some more info from Tripleplay. They also offered for the deal to cover two years at the same price. Take some time to review this but sounds like if you elect not to move forward, the system will still
 work, you just will not have access to tech support or any updates. Also I confirmed internally that the Tripleplay licenses on the server is good through August 23, 2032.
 
 
“The "Advanced Support" covers the full ecosystem of Tripleplay endpoints at the Star Complex. The EPG Data line item is for the “Electric Programming Guide” support.
 
The Advanced Support will cover ALL Tripleplay endpoints. We recognize that this number can fluctuate due to changes in the environment, so we have broadened the scope/description of the support to cover all the
 endpoints to not limit our team from providing any necessary and urgent support, i.e. they do not need to ask how many endpoints are currently in use, etc.
 
Without the support agreement, they are not receiving software updates or upgrades, bug fixes,  security patches, or troubleshooting assistance. This can leave the system exposed to malicious activity, etc. And
 they would be taking a risk without being security compliant.
 
Some of risks of lapsed or non-renewal of the support including:
 

?        
Loss of support and updates, including critical security patches

?        
Risk of blank screens or outdated content during network issues

?        
Reduced operational efficiency

?        
Potential non-compliance with encryption standards required in hospitality environments.
There is good reason to renew, especially with the June 2024 end-of-life (EOL) for CentOS 7. Since then, Uniguest has released Tripleplay 24.2, which supports Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 (RHEL 9).
 
More detail on the CentOS 7 end of life:
 
In June 2024, CentOS 7 went end of life, and since Uniguest released Tripleplay 24.2, which introduces support for a new OS, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9. 
 
Although existing CentOS 7 deployments will continue to be supported, to take advantage of the latest Tripleplay features and security improvements, platforms must be upgraded to Tripleplay 24.2 and Red Hat Enterprise
 Linux 9 or later. In particular:
 

As CentOS7 OS is officially end of life, it no longer receives official support, updates, or security patches.  It is therefore more at risk to security vulnerabilities, cyber threats, and operational issues.  It is unlikely that Uniguest will be able
 to mitigate such risks as Uniguest is severely constrained without official support from the CentOS project.  Over time as the regular updates stop and the level of community support decreases the level of risk will be further elevated for deployments that
 are on CentOS7.
 
RHEL has been selected as it benefits from enterprise-level support from a team of full-time engineers, keeping it well-maintained with frequent updates and stable and secure. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 will be supported until 2032.Being a modern OS, RHEL can
 take advantage of the latest hardware, e.g. CPU, GPU etc.
 
RHEL 9 is the latest version that provides a modern, functional OS that meets the Tripleplay platform's needs now and the future. As a newer technology, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 delivers enhanced security with SELinux improvements and newer cryptography support.
 Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 is already certified with major enterprise software providers. 

 
Platforms running Tripleplay 24.2 or newer also get access to the latest Tripleplay features and improvements; this gap will continue to widen with future updates, potentially reducing their deployment’s competitiveness and user satisfaction. For end users
 who have not upgraded since 23.1 was introduced, there is a huge step forward in user experience due to the UI redesign that was introduced at this time.
We strive to make our software as reliable and bug free as possible, however, bugs are a reality for software for all vendors. Regular updates mean you gain access to dozens of bug fixes which are incorporated into the product on an ongoing basis. This not
 only improves reliability but also improves user experience.

 
Note: For reference below are some current feature gaps in case any one of these is particularly relevant to Resorts World:

Increased IPTV Portal Editor flexibility with greater design and customization options.
New Parent Pages feature to make it quicker for Interactive TV Portal admins to create new pages by enabling common elements to be inherited by multiple other pages. 
Editable' Watch TV' elements to drive engagement and revenue through onscreen overlay components when viewing live TV. 
Support for Samsung Hospitality Tizen 7 for Interactive TV.
New Chromakey digital signage feature for customers utilizing BrightSign devices.
802.1x EAP-TLS certificate and key pairs can be uploaded to the server, making it easier for admins to manage and renew client device certificates.
 
Support is effectively “insurance”. When you need it,
you need it! And for the question of "what they would lose if they elected not to move forward?” It would be very unfortunate for the systems to go down or have a cyber security breach during peak times with customer/student engagement, etc.”

Chris

I wanted to provide an update following yesterday’s visit from the OES specialist.
 
Phil determined that the issue was the clock’s motherboard. He replaced the motherboard, and the clock is now functioning as intended. Phil took the faulty motherboard with him and will be sending it to OES
 for further investigation.

 purchasing a replacement. We are currently working on sourcing that replacement.
 
Given the visible burning on the digit and the fact that this is the second motherboard this clock has required, we believe there may be power surges contributing to these issues.

C            Aura Outfield Ribbon

Apologies for the delay—Peter has been out, and I’ve been connecting with the rest of the design team on this.

Our recommendation is to create one version for Board 2 and a different version for Board 3. We can reuse those storyboards for Boards 1 and 4. As Nicolette mentioned, we also recommend building a storyboard for Board 5.

  *   2280x480
  *   21360x720
  *   660x600
  *   214x1456
If you’d like multiple creative versions across Boards 6–18 and 20–22, we recommend supplying additional versions for the 2280x480 and 660x600 sizes.

We’ll need very flexible Adobe files for each storyboard so we can manipulate all sections and content as needed.

Please let us know if you have any questions.

I got some more info from Tripleplay. They also offered for the deal to cover two years at the same price. Take some time to review this but sounds like if you elect not to move forward, the system will still
 work, you just will not have access to tech support or any updates. Also I confirmed internally that the Tripleplay licenses on the server is good through August 23, 2032.
 
 
“The "Advanced Support" covers the full ecosystem of Tripleplay endpoints at the Star Complex. The EPG Data line item is for the “Electric Programming Guide” support.
 
The Advanced Support will cover ALL Tripleplay endpoints. We recognize that this number can fluctuate due to changes in the environment, so we have broadened the scope/description of the support to cover all the
 endpoints to not limit our team from providing any necessary and urgent support, i.e. they do not need to ask how many endpoints are currently in use, etc.
 
Without the support agreement, they are not receiving software updates or upgrades, bug fixes,  security patches, or troubleshooting assistance. This can leave the system exposed to malicious activity, etc. And
 they would be taking a risk without being security compliant.
 
Some of risks of lapsed or non-renewal of the support including:
 

·      
Loss of support and updates, including critical security patches

·      
Risk of blank screens or outdated content during network issues

·      
Reduced operational efficiency

·      
Potential non-compliance with encryption standards required in hospitality environments.
There is good reason to renew, especially with the June 2024 end-of-life (EOL) for CentOS 7. Since then, Uniguest has released Tripleplay 24.2, which supports Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 (RHEL 9).
 
More detail on the CentOS 7 end of life:
 
In June 2024, CentOS 7 went end of life, and since Uniguest released Tripleplay 24.2, which introduces support for a new OS, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9. 
 
Although existing CentOS 7 deployments will continue to be supported, to take advantage of the latest Tripleplay features and security improvements, platforms must be upgraded to Tripleplay 24.2 and Red Hat Enterprise
 Linux 9 or later. In particular:
 

As CentOS7 OS is officially end of life, it no longer receives official support, updates, or security patches.  It is therefore more at risk to security vulnerabilities, cyber threats, and operational issues.  It is unlikely that Uniguest will be able
 to mitigate such risks as Uniguest is severely constrained without official support from the CentOS project.  Over time as the regular updates stop and the level of community support decreases the level of risk will be further elevated for deployments that
 are on CentOS7.
 
RHEL has been selected as it benefits from enterprise-level support from a team of full-time engineers, keeping it well-maintained with frequent updates and stable and secure. Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 will be supported until 2032.Being a modern OS, RHEL can
 take advantage of the latest hardware, e.g. CPU, GPU etc.
 
RHEL 9 is the latest version that provides a modern, functional OS that meets the Tripleplay platform's needs now and the future. As a newer technology, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 delivers enhanced security with SELinux improvements and newer cryptography support.
 Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 is already certified with major enterprise software providers. 

 
Platforms running Tripleplay 24.2 or newer also get access to the latest Tripleplay features and improvements; this gap will continue to widen with future updates, potentially reducing their deployment’s competitiveness and user satisfaction. For end users
 who have not upgraded since 23.1 was introduced, there is a huge step forward in user experience due to the UI redesign that was introduced at this time.

We strive to make our software as reliable and bug free as possible, however, bugs are a reality for software for all vendors. Regular updates mean you gain access to dozens of bug fixes which are incorporated into the product on an ongoing basis. This not
 only improves reliability but also improves user experience.

 
Note: For reference below are some current feature gaps in case any one of these is particularly relevant to Resorts World:

Increased IPTV Portal Editor flexibility with greater design and customization options.
New Parent Pages feature to make it quicker for Interactive TV Portal admins to create new pages by enabling common elements to be inherited by multiple other pages. 
Editable' Watch TV' elements to drive engagement and revenue through onscreen overlay components when viewing live TV. 
Support for Samsung Hospitality Tizen 7 for Interactive TV.
New Chromakey digital signage feature for customers utilizing BrightSign devices.
802.1x EAP-TLS certificate and key pairs can be uploaded to the server, making it easier for admins to manage and renew client device certificates.
 
Support is effectively “insurance”. When you need it,
you need it! And for the question of "what they would lose if they elected not to move forward?” It would be very unfortunate for the systems to go down or have a cyber security breach during peak times with customer/student engagement, etc.”

Good Afternoon, 

I wanted to provide a recap of the work completed onsite in Charleston over the past two days.

On January 6, Ethan arrived onsite around 8:00 AM to install two new Nova VX400 processors. Both processors were fully configured with primary and backup settings, including network configuration.
 Livesync output was confirmed to be displaying correctly to the screen.

During testing, portions of the display showed intermittent signal loss. Ethan traced the issue to several CAT5 couplers in the signal path. Three couplers were replaced using the parts available
 onsite, which resolved the affected sections. Additional couplers were identified and are currently being shipped to site. As a temporary solution, the remaining couplers were bypassed, restoring full signal on the primary run.

On January 7, Ethan returned onsite while the client was present to test failover functionality and SDI feeds. The SDI feed was confirmed to be working as intended. During failover testing, it
 was observed that the backup processor was not receiving the correct Livesync signal. We worked with Allen from the school to trace the HDMI signal paths for both the primary and backup systems and identified a Gefen 4x4 in the signal chain that was no longer
 in use. After testing, the Gefen was determined to have nonfunctional ports.

To resolve this, the Master computer was configured to mirror outputs 2 and 3 directly to the primary and backup processors. Failover testing was then completed and confirmed that the Livesync
 signal does not drop during failover and that the system is operating as expected.

The workstation computer displaying the primary desktop instead of the backup has been corrected by swapping the cat5 cables on the back of the Draco KVM. 

Please let us know if you have any questions or would like us to follow up once the remaining couplers are replaced.

Below is a quick synopsis of why these new servers would alleviate issues at softball and baseball:

The existing servers supporting the baseball and softball systems are approximately 8–10 years old. The baseball system is still operating on Windows 7, and the softball system is running an older version of Windows 10. Both operating systems are no longer supported by Microsoft, which presents security, stability, and reliability concerns.
Due to the age of the hardware and operating systems, these servers are not capable of running the latest version of the LiveSync software, limiting functionality and long-term support.
Upgrading to new servers will allow us to:

  *   Utilize the current version of LiveSync
  *   Improve overall system stability and performance
Additionally, the new servers will include internal capture cards, eliminating the need for the existing BrightEye / TVOne scalers. This simplifies the signal chain and aligns the baseball and softball setups with the current soccer system configuration, which has proven to be stable and effective.

Subject: 51 Brookline - Weekly Meeting Minutes 1/8/26
Body:
Hi All, Wanted to capture our meeting minutes from yesterday’s meeting. Please review and let me know if I am missing anything or have any follow up questions/comments. Because of the concern of the current crane plan encroaching on the MBTA ZOI, it was suggested to install the vertical 60’ column in (2) separate 30’ pieces and splice these together in the field. This would require a smaller ton crane and ensure we stay out of the ZOI. LucentHD will determine if this is necessary with their contractors.LucentHD is currently looking to begin demo work on January 29th/30th. Demo will stop at the bottom angles that are penetrating the roof; ANC will work to have roofing contractor remove and patch these angles prior to mobilization.ANC needs a sample COI from OBM or needs to know who will be listed as the certificate holder to provide COIs from their subcontractors prior to mobilization. Gemma, Thanks for the call and follow up yesterday. Below is a top line breakout that summarizes our bid proposal.  Note that our proposal is fixed and final and protects MSGE from any Change Orders from the Base Contract deliverables.  In regard to the largest line items (labor ), we bid with North Shore as they were the contractor that worked for Vornado at 2 Penn and have the firsthand knowledge and experience of the conditions and the electrical and data routing.   As I shared, since our initial 2024 bid the Union contract was renewed with a 10% increase.  ANC is honoring our original pricing without the Union increase to MSG.  Also from our experience, there are only two (2) installers that are qualified to do the Union work.  North Shore Neon and AMA.  There are others, but these are the known providers in NYC. In addition to the offering, ANC is extending the same service and support that we are providing at Moynihan Train Hall to MSGE at no additional cost for the duration of the Moynihan Train Hall SLA or a minimum of two (2) years.  Whichever is favorable to MSGE. OVERALL SUMMARY ElementExt $3.9mm Bulkhead Displays$165,910Structural Labor$649,505.56Electrical and Data $90,000Project Management and General Conditions$7,732Engineering$33,333 ALTERNATES ElementExt $Option 1:  Twelve (12) 1.5mm Recessed Wall Displays$56,883Option 2: Change LED VIP Wall to LG86H5F-M LCD Displays($153,778)ALT 1: Change Bulkhead displays to 6mm($13,591)  ELECTRICAL BREAKOUT Union labor Both the power and low voltage work is a long run and travels through finished spaces and ceilingsSpecialized lifts and equipment (portion appropriated to the electric / low voltage work)In Vornado areas, we have to adhere to their requirements (e.g., protective flooring)Work hours and access ElementEstimated ValuesElectrical Labor Large Displays$33,500Electrical Labor – Ground Level Displays$12,500Low Voltage Labor -  Large Displays$9,111Low Voltage Labor – Ground Level Displays$5,333Materials, Cables, Interconnects, Rack Equipment, Misc$15,861Integration, Commissioning and Ceterification$13,695  Call me with any questions.  Here to help in any way. Alex     Alex GomezSVP, RelationshipsM: (917) 547-9499alexg@anc.com

Description:
To: aram.hong@lge.com
CC: shj2011.jung@lge.com; alexg@anc.com; yohan1.choi@lge.com; jh818.lee@lge.com; kylek.park@lge.com; dohan2.lee@lge.com
BCC: 
Attachment: --none--

Subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] Re: Thank You/Information from Meeting/Next Steps
Body:
Aram,Thank you for the time, consideration, and openness throughout this process. While we’re naturally disappointed not to be moving forward together at this location, we completely understand the decision and appreciate the thoughtful evaluation behind it.We recognize that comparing an existing installation to renderings can be challenging, and that the reasoning behind your decision is sound. From our experience, we’ve often seen perceptions evolve once a sign is fully realized and activated in-market.As you finalize terms to remain at the current location, we would simply encourage keeping some flexibility in place, if possible.  We may surprise you all with the final product and it could prompt a desire to move.   With our long-term partnerships, we typically allow clients optional termination windows at certain points in the contract and assume the current operator would do the same.We also wanted to share to bring up a fee things.We understand LG is exploring being a provider in outdoor advertising space.  Should there be interest, we would be open to exploring the use of LG product (steep discount) at our  location, potentially positioning it as a high-profile showcase in Times Square.  This could also make the a possibility moving to a location that has your technology. 제목: Thank You/Information from Meeting/Next Steps Evening All,It was a true pleasure meeting all of you. Thank you again for visiting our office and taking the time to discuss the possibility of creating a new home for LG in Times Square. I sincerely appreciated the thoughtful conversation and the opportunity to learn more about your thoughts on the current sign and to share our vision for a potential new one.LG’s long history in Times Square is deeply meaningful, and we would be honored to support you in shaping the next chapter. After our meeting, I shared with my family how special this project feels to us — including stories from my father about my grandfather’s work on the Gold Star sign.I understand this is an important and complex decision. Please know that we are here to support you as you evaluate all possible scenarios — even if that ultimately includes considering another location. Our goal is to be a thoughtful and reliable partner throughout your process, wherever it leads.Below is a list of the materials we reviewed during our meeting, along with a few additional photos and videos that may be helpful as you continue your internal discussions.Projection Sketch – This provides a bird’s-eye view of the proposed projection of the Led sign. I don’t think we need to run the Led sign as far down the street as the rendering depicts. Building Simulation Rendering   - Shows how the new sign will fit to scale within the current landscape. If we move forward, I think we should capture this from additional angles. Video Simulation 1  & Video Simulation 2  - Shows still Led sign video renderings from two different angles.  We can work on this video from different angles.  Are there areas you would like to see it from? Current Sign 1 , Current Sign 2, Current Sign 3 , Current Sign 4, Current Sign 5  - Images of the current sign from different points in Duffy Square are attached. We’ll put together additional photos next week. These photos show that even though the current sign isn’t digital, it still stands out in the square because of how low it sits to the ground. Once converted to digital, the unit will have an even stronger presence in Duffy Square. Photo of NYE 2024.jpg – Shows a photo of the main stage next to the proposed location. 2025 Video of Ball Drop – Ball drop view from Duffy Square that shows the tv production and stage area.  One thing I forgot to touch on is how having the sign positioned lower to the ground creates opportunities for interactivity. One idea is to designate specific spots where people can stand and manipulate the creative or play motion-based games on the display. This would work by mounting cameras at the bottom of the sign, focused on these designated points. When someone steps into one of those spots, they can interact with the digital display during scheduled activation times. Our team is going to work on some other materials to share.  Is there any other information you would like to know about the proposed location please let me know. Hope you all had good trips back home and I look forward to discussing this project further with all of you. With Gratitude,James    James Manfredi

Overall the project is creating 42,000+ jobs, which will create a ton of additional traffic in and around the area, and there could be some unique ways to create a marketing/sponsorship partnership to drive awareness and trust for BILT, while also tapping into the affordable housing and overall mixed-use development. Does this help?
